title: The Horizon of Sector Nine
premise: Juniper Yarrow, the last xenolinguist on Meridian Station, has spent nine years maintaining a beacon whose original commission records were erased—along with every trace of the colony that once lived in Sector Nine. When the station's children begin dreaming identical dreams in a language only Juniper can parse, she realizes the beacon isn't transmitting to deep space; it's broadcasting the memories of the dead into young minds. As the reactor begins an unexplained countdown and the station's administrator moves to silence the children, Juniper must reconstruct the Sector Nine massacre from dream-fragments alone, knowing the truth will cost her the loyalty of everyone she loves. In the end, she broadcasts the children's testimony through the beacon itself, choosing justice over survival as the countdown reaches zero—and the reactor, revealed as the colonists' memorial engine, finally goes dark at peace.
about_author: Ivo Sandoval is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years at a remote listening post before turning to fiction. Their work explores what survives of us in signals, and they write from a cabin with no internet connection.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She performs her lonely maintenance rounds on the beacon, decoding its strange recurring pulse while the station above her ignores her existence. A child named Wren appears at her door, speaking a phrase no human tongue should know. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine—the first crack in her carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Shared Sleep
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The children of Meridian gather secretly to compare dreams: the same burning corridor, the same locked door, the same word repeated. Wren seeks out Juniper because adults dismiss them. Emotional beat: the eerie solidarity of children carrying something too heavy, and the thrill of being believed for the first time.

chapters.title: A Language Without Speakers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She translates the dream-word and recognizes it as structural xenoglossy—grammar from a civilization that never existed in any archive. Cross-referencing the beacon's pulse, she finds timestamps matching a gap in station history. Emotional beat: scholarly wonder curdling into horror as the erasure reveals itself as deliberate.

chapters.title: Administrator Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The station administrator notices power anomalies around the beacon and orders Juniper to justify its existence. Charming and reasonable, he offers her promotion if she shuts it down. Emotional beat: the seductive comfort of authority, and Juniper's realization that Voss may not know what he's protecting—or may know exactly.

chapters.title: Sector Nine
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following dream-coordinates, she breaches a sealed habitat ring and finds scorch patterns, child-sized doorframes, and a wall of names scratched from inside. The reactor's countdown begins the moment she crosses the threshold. Emotional beat: grief arriving like a physical blow; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Juniper and Voss. Voss presents flawless official logs proving Sector Nine never existed; Juniper realizes the falsification is generations old, woven into the station's founding data. Loyal crew members begin avoiding her. Emotional beat: isolation deepening—the loneliness of holding evidence no one wants to be true.

chapters.title: The Children's Testimony
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The dreams intensify; the children begin sleepwalking toward the sealed ring. Wren organizes them to record their shared visions before the administrator can medicate them. Emotional beat: fierce courage—children becoming witnesses, transforming passive haunting into deliberate testimony.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With three days left, she decodes the reactor's countdown as part of the beacon's message: a deadline set by the dying colonists, demanding acknowledgment or erasure completed. Voss locks down the station and detains Wren. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve; loyalty to the living now demands betraying their comfort.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, climax. She fights her way to the beacon array with the children's recorded testimony, uploads the translated massacre record, and transmits it to every colony in range as the countdown hits zero. Voss's enforcers arrive seconds too late. Emotional beat: triumphant sacrifice—truth spoken at the exact cost of everything safe.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Juniper and Wren's alternating POV. The reactor powers down gently, a memorial fulfilled rather than a weapon detonated. Outside colonies respond with investigators, apologies, indictments. The children stop dreaming—but Wren keeps one phrase, spoken freely now. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; justice outside the law achieved, and grief finally allowed to become memory.
